greet: Come near, my pikin. Dis na our clay pot. We dey call am ikoko.
greet.ask: Wetin dem dey call the pot?
made: One potter mould am with hand from river clay, then bake am inside open fire until e strong.
made.ask: How dem dey make the pot?
old: Women for dis land don dey mould pot like dis for thousands of years. Dem dey find the broken pieces for where the oldest towns bin dey before.
potters: The work dey pass from mama to im daughter. Every potter get her own mark, so you fit know whose hand make one pot.
mother: Dis one na my mama own. She dey carry water with am from river for her head, and she give am to me for my wedding day.
water: We dey keep our drinking water inside am. The clay dey breathe, so the water dey cold, even for afternoon.
cook: Another pot like dis dey sidon on top three stones for fire, and our soup dey cook inside am.
cook.ask: Wetin una dey cook inside am?
care: Carry am gently, hold am with your two hands. Clay pot wey fall no dey stand up again.
